The file works because each compiler treats the same lines differently:
- **Line splicing:** The first line is `//\`. C++ splices the backslash-newline, so the Rust `main` on line 2 becomes part of a comment. Rust treats `//\` as an ordinary comment, so line 2 is code.
- **Nested comments:** `/* /*` opens a block comment in both compilers. The following `*/` closes it in C++, so the C++ code after it is live. Rust supports nested block comments, so it stays inside the comment until the final `// */`. That hides the C++ code from Rust.

Both versions use 64-bit unsigned integers, so the result overflows past f(91). Say if you want larger values; 128-bit integers would extend the range.
